title: A forge merges every open merge request: no file that every record shares
objective: Creating or changing one thread, work package or issue writes no file that another record's change also writes, so a forge merges any number of open merge requests with no hand step (issue 0705, hv decision 66).
context:
Issue 0705, measured on brew 3.4.0 on 2026-11-19: once one merge request lands, a forge can merge none of the others, because creating a record or changing its status rewrites `intent/.intentfiles`, `intent/st/steel_threads.md` and `intent/todo.md` at the same place on every branch. ST0095 makes ids unique by construction, and leaves these three files as the one hand step left in a review-gated flow.

hv decision 66 rules the fix: the two generated lists leave git, and whether a record is realised is carried by the record or derived from its status, so no shared manifest is written. hv decision 67 asks for a very thorough Highlander check, which runs as vc decision 133 says. The design, with the measurements, is `design.md`. The same work rides the same release as ST0095, and its first package shares ST0095's schema bump.

wps.title: Realisation lives in the record, and the manifest goes
wps.objective: Whether a thread or an issue is realised on disk is answered by the record, by one owner, and `intent/.intentfiles` is folded into the records and removed by `intent upgrade`.
wps.body:
Seat: cc. Size: M. Lands after ST0095's WP-06, whose schema bump it shares, so a project migrates its canon once.

## Scope

- **cc chooses R1 or R2** (design.md, "Realisation leaves the shared manifest") and writes the choice and its reason into the design before any code (AC-01.3). R1: the record carries whether it is realised. R2: realisation is derived from status, and a record carries an override only when a person hydrated or dehydrated it against the default.
- **One owner of realisation.** One module answers whether a record is realised, and organize, hydrate, dehydrate, sync, doctor and the views ask it.
- **The verbs that change realisation write it on their own record only**: `st start`, `st hold`, `st resume`, `st done`, `st hydrate`, `st dehydrate`, `issues add` and `issues close` (the census in design.md).
- **`intent upgrade` folds `.intentfiles` into the records and removes the file**, byte-deterministically, in the same mechanical change as ST0095's format rewrite.
- **ST0095's WP-05**: whether its `.intentfiles` set merge and its regeneration of the two lists stay, cc's call (design.md, "What this changes in ST0095"), recorded in both threads, with issue 0704's disposition.

## Out of scope

- The two lists leaving git (WP-02).
- Two merge requests that change one thread (design.md, "The case that remains"), unless hv rules otherwise at review.

## Proof

- AC-01.1's test, over every verb in the census's table.
- AC-01.2's test: the fold is byte-deterministic, and a project upgraded on two branches apart merges clean.
- A critic-rust review of the diff, each Highlander finding fixed or answered (AC-00.2).

wps.title: The two lists leave git
wps.objective: `intent/st/steel_threads.md` and `intent/todo.md` are rendered on disk as today and are never tracked: a new project ignores them, and `intent upgrade` takes an existing project's copies out of git's index once.
wps.body:
Seat: ic, with cc on what `intent upgrade` means. Size: M. Lands after nothing; it can start in ic's slack before ST0095's WP-10.

## Scope

- **`intent init` ignores both lists**, through the writer that writes `intent/.cache/` and `intent/.backup/` into `.gitignore` today.
- **`intent upgrade` adds the same two lines to an existing project's `.gitignore`** and takes both files out of git's index, leaving them on disk, in the one mechanical change the upgrade already makes. Its output names every path it changed.
- **The set of generated aggregate views is declared once**, and init, upgrade, doctor and the commit gate (WP-03) read it.
- **doctor names a project whose lists are still tracked**, with `intent upgrade` as the fix, as an advisory that is not counted, as cc's meaning for a project in today's format says (design.md).
- **The verbs and `intent sync` keep rendering both lists on disk**, so `intent st list`, `intent todo` and a person reading the files see what they see today.
- From the Highlander sweep (vc decision 133, report A at `refs/bank/vc/st0095/highlander-A-intentsvcs-20261119`): `todo_update` writes `todo.md` by a second route (`facade.rs:13394`, `13479`). One writer, with cc.

## Out of scope

- Realisation (WP-01). The commit gate and the pull-request check (WP-03).
- The docs, which ride ST0095's WP-13.

## Proof

- AC-02.1's and AC-02.2's tests.
- A critic-rust review of the diff, each Highlander finding fixed or answered (AC-00.2).

wps.title: The commit gate and the pull-request check follow
wps.objective: The repository's commit gate and pull-request check work on a project whose two lists are tracked and on one whose lists are not, and read the lists' paths from the one declared set.
wps.body:
Seat: dc. Size: S. Lands after WP-02.

## Scope

- **The checks that compare committed views with the model** (eg `thread_view_skew_check.sh`) no longer expect the two lists in git once a project is upgraded, and still judge them where a project has not been.
- **Any check, workflow or smoke that names a list by path** reads the declared set from WP-02 instead of its own copy of the path.
- **This repository's own lists leave git at its post-cut upgrade**, with every other estate, because vc decision 132 keeps the main checkout in today's format until the release is installed from brew. Nothing here untracks them by hand.

- **The gate's own reader of `.intentfiles` goes with the file** (vc's Highlander sweep, report C, cluster A, folded in by dc). `canon_commit_check.sh:228-233` is gated and live today. It ignores `ISSUE` rows, and it reads a present zero-byte file as everything realised, where the Rust parser and the file's own header read it as keep nothing. It reads the declared set from WP-02 instead.
- **The by-hand copies are not routed but retired** in dc's separate proposal, since no gate, CI step or bats test runs them: `realise_plan.sh:92-110` (a grammar that accepts region markers no grammar has), `:56-66` and `:176-189` (its own declaration rule), and ST0057's `sparse_tree_equals_manifest.sh:141-160`, which aborts on `ISSUE` rows and so refuses this repository's own manifest (clusters A and B).

## Out of scope

- The verbs (WP-01, WP-02). The proof rig (WP-04).

## Proof

- AC-03.1's test.
- A critic-shell review of the diff, and critic-rust if the diff touches Rust, each Highlander finding fixed or answered (AC-00.2).

wps.title: The proof: five merge requests through a forge stand-in
wps.objective: Five merge requests opened from one main merge one after another as a forge merges them, with no conflict and no hand step.
wps.body:
Seat: dc. Size: S. Lands after WP-01 and WP-02, and so after ST0095's WP-06.

## Scope

- **One test, on the rig of ST0095's two-clone test.** Five merge requests opened from one main, in two clones and two worktrees. Each one creates and starts a thread, adds a work package and adds an issue.
- **Each is merged in turn by a bare repository's `git merge-tree --write-tree`**, which is how a forge merges, with no `.gitattributes` merge driver and no `intent` run on the forge side.
- **After a pull of each merge**: `intent doctor` is clean, and both lists name every record.
- It runs in the cut's gate.

## Out of scope

- Two merge requests that change one thread (design.md, "The case that remains").

## Proof

- AC-04.1's test, run once by dc and read by vc.
- A critic review of the diff for each language it touches (AC-00.2).

wps.title: Each work package, criterion and test has its own canon file
wps.objective: Two merge requests that change the same thread merge on a forge with no hand step: each work package, criterion and test lives in its own canon file, and the thread's views are laid out so that no two of them share a file (hv decision 70).
wps.body:
- **Why**: a thread's canon is one file today, `intent/.canon/st/<id>.json`, holding its packages, criteria, tests and attachments, and its `info.md` and `acceptance.md` list them all. So two merge requests that each add a work package, a criterion or a test to one thread conflict there. hv decision 70 closes this in this release, against vc's recommendation, and hv decision 71 starts the thread.
- **Its meaning is cc's, and the views' shape ic's.** cc designs the split after ST0095 WP-04 lands: how a thread's canon divides, how the split rides ST0095's schema change so that a project migrates once, and what `intent upgrade` does to an existing thread. ic says how the thread views divide so that no two records share one. vc writes the design into `design.md` before any code, with this package's criteria, its size, and whether the views need a package of their own.
- **It lands before WP-04**, whose proof carries the same-thread case (AC-04.2).

criteria.text: Highlander, as hv decision 67 asks: at the close, an independent sweep finds one owner of realisation, one writer of the ignore lines and one declared set of generated aggregate views, in every language, and every finding of the sweep of the existing code made at the start (its .intentfiles and aggregate-view sections) is resolved in the package that owns it or answered on the record.

Highlander on every change, as hv decision 67 asks: every unit of this thread lands with a critic-<lang> review of its diff for each language the diff touches, each Highlander finding fixed or answered, read by vc against the diff before land.
Every verb in design.md's census table writes no file outside the thread or issue it changes: that record's canon file, its events and its realised views.
intent upgrade folds intent/.intentfiles into the records and removes it, byte-deterministically, so a project upgraded on two branches apart merges clean.
The design records cc's choice between R1 and R2 with its reason before WP-01's code starts, with the disposition of ST0095 WP-05's .intentfiles set merge and of issue 0704.

criteria.text: A new project and an upgraded one keep intent/st/steel_threads.md, intent/todo.md and every thread's intent/st/<ST>/acceptance.md on disk and out of git, and the verbs and intent sync keep them current.
doctor names a project whose aggregate views (the two lists, or any thread's acceptance.md) are still tracked, with intent upgrade as the fix, as an advisory that is not counted.

doctor shows an ignored aggregate view that is missing, or that differs from what the store renders, with intent sync --to-disk as the fix, and counts neither, so a fresh clone's first commit passes the commit gate; a view still tracked is counted as today.

The repository's commit gate and pull-request check pass on a project with its aggregate views (the two lists and every thread's acceptance.md) tracked and on one with them untracked, and read their paths from the one declared set.

Five merge requests opened from one main, in two clones and two worktrees, each creating and starting a thread and adding a work package and an issue, merge in turn by a bare repository's merge as a forge merges, with no conflict, and intent doctor is clean after each is pulled.

Two merge requests opened from one main that change one thread, one adding a work package and the other a criterion and a test, merge in turn by a bare repository's merge as a forge merges, with no conflict, and intent doctor is clean after each is pulled.

A thread's canon in the release's format is one file for the thread's own fields and one file per work package, criterion, test and attachment under .canon/records/<thread>/, each named by its record's stored id or label, and no file lists, counts or orders a thread's children: the thread's records directory holds them, read in the waist's order.

Two branches from one base, one adding a work package to a thread and the other adding a criterion and a test to the same thread, change disjoint files, and git merges them with no conflict; intent doctor is clean on the merge. (dc's AC-04.2 proves the same through the forge stand-in; this is the unit's own two-branch test.)

intent upgrade moves an existing thread to that layout byte-for-byte the same on two clones upgraded apart, and changes no id and no value; no committed view is rendered from more than one record, so the cover renders only the thread's own fields (hv decision 74); the closed records' views still committed on main are removed by the upgrade under removed:; an attachment whose bytes on disk differ from canon is refused by name and never removed; and a canon case pair (two attachments whose paths differ only in case, issue 0722) is refused by name before the split, since a folding disk would put both in one canon file.

attachments.text:
# Design: a forge merges every open merge request with no hand step

**Status: under way since 2026-11-19 11:38Z by vc's date -u, on hv's go (hv decision 71).** hv decision 66 rules the direction, hv decision 67 the Highlander check, and hv decision 70 brings the same-thread case into this release. Written by vc from its own measurements on brew 3.4.0. A claim says whether it was measured or read. The defect is issue 0705.

## The problem, measured

Once ST0095 lands, two branches never mint the same id. They still both write three files that every record shares, so on a forge the first merge request to land blocks every other one that is open.

- **The reproduction** (vc, 2026-11-19, brew 3.4.0, banked under `refs/bank/vc/st0095/drive-*`): five branches each minted and started a thread from one main, and a second clone merged them as a forge's merge button does. After the first merge, none of the other four merged. Each conflicted with main in `intent/.intentfiles`, `intent/st/steel_threads.md` and `intent/todo.md`.
- **The census** (vc, 2026-11-19, brew 3.4.0): every lifecycle verb run in a scratch project, each change committed on its own, and the files it changed listed. The shared files each verb writes:

| Verb                                          | `.intentfiles` | `steel_threads.md` | `todo.md` |
| --------------------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------ | --------- |
| `st new`                                      |                | yes                | yes       |
| `st start`, `st hold`, `st resume`, `st done` | yes            | yes                | yes       |
| `wp new`, `wp start`, `wp done`               |                |                    | yes       |
| `issues add`, `issues close`                  | yes            |                    |           |
| `st hydrate`, `st dehydrate`                  | yes            |                    |           |
| `ac new`, `ac satisfy`, `at new`              |                |                    |           |

Every other file a verb writes belongs to one record: its canon file, its event file and its realised views. There is no aggregate list of issues, since each issue has its own view.

- **git's union merge driver is no fix** (vc, 2026-11-19, git 2.56.1). Declared in `.gitattributes`, it resolves both kinds of file in a working tree's `git merge`. A bare repository's `git merge-tree --write-tree`, which is how a forge merges, ignores it unless `attr.tree` or `--attr-source` is set, and only the forge's configuration decides that.

## The ruling

hv decision 66: a forge merges any number of open merge requests with no hand step, by construction. So creating or changing one record writes no file that another record's change also writes:

1. **The two generated lists leave git.** Every clone renders them from its own store.
2. **Realisation stops being one shared manifest.** Whether a record is on disk is carried by the record or derived from its status.

The alternative, keeping the files with one hand step per merge request, is not taken.

## The design

### The two lists leave git (ic, with cc on what upgrade does)

- `intent/st/steel_threads.md` and `intent/todo.md` are still rendered on disk by the verbs that change them and by `intent sync`. Their content does not change.
- **A new project ignores them.** `intent init` writes both into `.gitignore` beside `intent/.cache/` and `intent/.backup/`, through the writer that writes those lines today.
- **An existing project stops tracking them once.** `intent upgrade` adds the two lines to `.gitignore` and takes both files out of git's index, leaving them on disk. It is one mechanical change, committed with the rest of the upgrade.
- **doctor names a project whose lists are still tracked**, with `intent upgrade` as the fix, as an advisory that is not counted. That follows cc's meaning for a project in today's format, given for ST0095 on 2026-11-19: such a project is consistent and readable and only cannot mint yet, so the new build works on it and refuses only the first mint, with `intent upgrade` as the one remedy.
- **What a reader loses**: the forge's web view no longer shows the two lists. Each realised thread's `info.md` and each issue's view stay tracked, so a thread or an issue is still readable on the forge. The index of them is not.
- **A thread's `acceptance.md` leaves git too** (hv decision 74, 2026-11-20, on ic's and cc's position). It is rendered from every criterion and test of its thread, so it joins the declared set as `intent/st/*/acceptance.md`: `intent init` ignores it, `intent upgrade` untracks it, and doctor's advisory names it. No package of ic's is needed. A split into a file per criterion and test was not taken: it would cost an M package and a tracked file per record, and it still could not show a test-backed criterion's verdict, which is computed from its tests. The forge then no longer shows a thread's criteria and tests as a page, nor, once WP-05 lands, the cover's package table. It still shows the cover's objective and context, each package's own view, the attachments and each record's canon JSON.
- **Every planner still sees the aggregate views** (cc's meaning, 2026-11-20, on ic's design point from WP-02's critic review). `.gitignore` says what git tracks, never what Intent owns. The planners' corpus (sync's scan, which organize, sync, hydrate and dehydrate plan from) reads the one declared set whatever an ignore rule says. So the plan sees a realised thread's `acceptance.md`, removes a closed thread's and re-renders a stale list, as AC-02.1 says. Nothing else an ignore rule hides joins the corpus.
- **doctor counts no ignored aggregate view** (cc's meaning, 2026-11-20; AC-02.3). An ignored view is the clone's own rendering of its store, like `intent/.cache/`, and a fresh clone has none. doctor shows one that is missing, or that differs from what the store renders, with `intent sync --to-disk` as the fix, and counts neither, since a commit carries neither. A view still tracked, in a project not yet upgraded, is counted as today, because a commit does carry it. Nothing renders a view on open: a read writes nothing.

### Realisation leaves the shared manifest (cc)

Today `intent/.intentfiles` lists each realised record as a row, `STEELTHREAD:ST0095` or `ISSUE:0704` (read: `intentfiles.rs:106-121`), and its header says a row is state, never regenerated from status. The verbs in the table above rewrite it.

There are two ways to make it per record, and the choice is cc's call on meaning:

| Option                        | What a record carries                                                         | Which verbs write realisation                                                                    | What changes in meaning                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| R1, the record carries it     | whether it is realised                                                        | every verb in the `.intentfiles` column, each on its own record, which all but two already write | nothing: realisation stays state                                                                                            |
| R2, derived, with an override | an override, only when a person hydrated or dehydrated it against the default | `st hydrate` and `st dehydrate` only                                                             | the default becomes a function of status: a WIP thread or an OPEN issue is realised, as `organize --default` computes today |

- **cc chose R1** on 2026-11-19 (AC-01.3). In cc's words: realisation is state today, not a function of status. Every transition verb edits it, and each takes `ListEdit::{AsDeclared, Suppressed}`, so a caller can move a thread's status and leave its realisation alone. R1 moves that state from one shared file into each record with no change in meaning, and upgrade's fold maps rows to records exactly: a listed record carries `realised: true`, and the field is absent otherwise. R2 would change meaning one of two ways: either an override outlives a transition, so a thread once dehydrated stays dehydrated after `st reopen`, which realises it today, or each transition clears it, which is R1's state under another name. R1's writes all fall on the record each verb already writes, except `st hydrate` and `st dehydrate`, which now write their thread's canon instead of the manifest.
- **Either way `.intentfiles` goes.** `intent upgrade` folds its rows into the records and removes it. The fold is byte-deterministic, so two branches upgraded apart merge clean.
- **It rides ST0095's schema bump.** ST0095 already gives the thread and issue canon a new schema version. With this field in the same unreleased version, a project migrates its canon once.
- **Not taken: keeping `.intentfiles` for overrides only.** A rare conflict is still a hand step.

### What this changes in ST0095

- **ST0095's WP-05 merges `.intentfiles` as a set, and regenerates the two lists in a conflicted merge**, which closes issue 0704. In a project this thread has upgraded, neither file is in git, so neither conflict occurs. A branch cut before the upgrade upgrades before it merges (ST0095's design, "Upgrading a project", point 3), so the set merge has no case left. cc dropped both on 2026-11-19 (AC-01.3): WP-05 goes from M to S, AC-05.2 is withdrawn, and issue 0704 is superseded by this thread and closes when it lands. A merge of two branches both still in today's format meets the conflict it meets today, and `intent upgrade` is that state's one remedy.
- **ST0095's WP-13** (ic) carries this thread's docs: the team page's merge sections are rewritten once, for both threads.
- **ST0095's brew smoke and drill** (dc's WP-03 and WP-12) run with the two lists untracked once this thread has landed.

### Two merge requests that change one thread: closed in this release (WP-05)

- **Measured**: `wp new`, `wp start`, `wp done`, the `ac` and `at` verbs and the thread's own lifecycle verbs all write the thread's canon file and its realised views. Two merge requests that change one thread meet there.
- After ST0095 the ids inside never collide, so `intent sync --apply --yes` keeps both sides. A forge cannot run it, so today such a merge request takes one hand step: merge main, run the sync, commit and push.
- **hv decision 70 closes it by construction in this release**, against vc's recommendation to leave it: each work package, criterion and test gets its own canon file, and the thread views are laid out so that no two of them share one. That is a second change to the canon's layout and a rewrite of the thread views, L to XL, on cc's chain, so it moves the release.
- **cc's design is the next section**, given on 2026-11-19 after ST0095 WP-04 landed. ic says how the views divide.

### Each record its own canon file (WP-05; cc's meaning, 2026-11-19)

- **One canon file per record.** The thread keeps `intent/.canon/st/<thread>.json` with its own fields only: schema, id, origin, title, slug, status, created, completed, objective, context, body, preamble, related and realised. Each work package goes to `intent/.canon/records/<thread>/wp/<wp>.json`, each criterion to `.../ac/<label>.json`, each test to `.../at/<label>.json`, and each attachment's record to `.../attachments/<path>.json`. Attachments go too, beyond hv decision 70's three kinds, because they sit inline in the thread file today, so two merge requests that edit different attachments of one thread would still meet there. Issues keep `intent/.canon/issues/<issue>.json`.
- **The records have a root of their own (cc, 2026-11-20, on critic-rust's finding against WP-05 A1).** An opaque attachment's bytes stay at `intent/.canon/st/<thread>/<path>`, as 3.4.0 keeps them, and nothing else lives there. Putting the record directories inside that directory let an attachment's path land on a record: an opaque `wp/notes.json` read back as a work package, a file named `wp` against the directory, or `WP/03/diagram.png` inside `wp/` on a disk that folds case. Reserving the four names was rejected because it would refuse an image under `WP/`, Intent's own convention. With two roots the collision cannot happen, so nothing refuses it. What remains is two attachments whose paths differ only in case (issue 0722), which the writer refuses.
- **A thread's file says its own layout.** A reader takes the children from the record files when the thread's file is in the release's format, by the schema the file carries rather than `project.json`'s. `intent upgrade` writes each thread's records before its own file, and `project.json` last, so an upgrade cut short reads back whole and runs again.
- **The name is the key, and nothing lists the children.** A file is named by its record's stored id, or a criterion or test by its label. No file holds an array of a thread's children, counts them or orders them: they are what the thread's records directory, `intent/.canon/records/<thread>/`, holds, read in the waist's order (ordinals by number, hashed records by origin).
- **What stays shared is shared by meaning.** Two merge requests that edit one record, eg both change a thread's objective, still meet in that record's file. That is a real conflict, as it is for one issue today.
- **A view rendered from more than one record cannot stay in git.** Today two are: the cover's work-package table and `acceptance.md`. The cover renders only the thread's own fields, and its Acceptance and Work Packages sections say where to read the rest (`intent ac list <ST>`, `intent wp list <ST>`), in ic's wording. `acceptance.md` leaves git like the two lists (hv decision 74). A package's `WP/<id>/info.md` already renders only its package.
- **One canon version for the release, so a project migrates once.** The store migrates itself on open, per machine; the canon migrates by `intent upgrade`, once per project, committed. The first of ST0095 WP-06 and this thread's WP-01 and WP-05 to land bumps the canon format, and the others amend that same unreleased version in place. That is safe because no released build writes the intermediate shape and no canon on main carries it: main is upgraded at the cut, and the drill runs on a clone.
- **`intent upgrade` is one function from 3.4.0's format to the release's**, extended by each package: ids as strings (ST0095 WP-06), the `.intentfiles` fold (WP-01), the split (WP-05) and the two lists untracked (WP-02). It is byte-deterministic, so two branches upgraded apart merge clean, and idempotent. It prints every path under `wrote:` and `removed:`, and writes `project.json`'s schema last, so an interrupted upgrade leaves the project unmarked and re-runnable. Before it runs, the new build reads and writes today's layout for every write but a mint (hv decision 70), choosing the layout in one place by `project.json`'s schema.
- **On an existing thread**, eg ST0095, the upgrade rewrites the thread file with its own fields and `realised: true`, writes `wp/01.json` to `wp/14.json` (`seq: 4` becomes `id: "04"`) and one file for each criterion, test and attachment. It changes no id and no value besides those spellings, and the store needs no rebuild, since it already holds one row per record. For an all-ordinal project, every view that keeps its layout is byte-identical.
- **The 22 closed records still on disk go.** Main commits the views of 21 closed issues and the realised tree of completed ST0093, none declared in `.intentfiles`, because closing took each row out and left its views. Every fresh clone's `sync` already plans to remove them, brew 3.4.0's included. R1's fold maps the manifest exactly, so the upgrade removes them in its own commit, under `removed:`. Nothing is lost, since each is rendered from the store or carried in canon. An attachment whose bytes on disk differ from canon (an edit never synced) is refused by name, never removed.
- **Size and order**: L, after ST0095 WP-06. cc builds ST0095 WP-05 and WP-06's canon change so that the split extends it: id and origin go on the record structs, which later move whole into their own files.
